Tina — attaching a network diagram (network_diagram_v2.png) and a short technical summary. Highlights below: 

1) Egress model
- Default: customer-controlled egress via an operator-configurable NAT/egress gateway. The Private deployment control plane can be deployed with either:
  a) Fully isolated mode (no outbound connectivity; updates and telemetry pulled/pushed via an approved jump host or offline media) or
  b) Customer-managed egress with allow-list to Redwood endpoints (for optional telemetry/alerts).
- Required firewall rules for customer-managed mode: outbound TCP 443 to the following FQDNs and IP ranges (we provide a compact list in Appendix A). No inbound ports are opened by Redwood.

2) Network segmentation
- Control plane, runtime nodes, and operator workstation zones are segmented. Inter-zone traffic uses mTLS with mutual certs we provide as part of the installation bundle.

3) Maintenance & upgrade pathways
- For fully air-gapped installs we support signed upgrade bundles delivered via removable media. For VPC installs we use HTTPS with artifact signing verification.

Notes: see attached diagram for the operator jump host pattern and a sample firewall rule set.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: network_diagram_v2.png (diagram), RFI_Starlab_Appendix_A.pdf (evidence appendix)

Tina — adding KMS/HSM and supply-chain details. Key points: 

- KMS options:
  * Customer-managed KMS (recommended): Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS, or on-prem HSM) using standard KMIP or native provider APIs. Keys never leave the customer's control plane.
  * Redwood-managed HSM (optional for Dedicated deployments): HSM-backed key protection where keys are stored in a FIPS 140-2 validated HSM managed under our MSP (requires contractual terms).

- Where keys are used: Data-at-rest encryption keys are held in the customer KMS; per-tenant runtime keys used for ephemeral session encryption are derived and rotated locally. We provide workflows for key rotation and emergency key revocation in the operator runbook.

- SBOM & signed artifacts:
  * We provide a reproducible SBOM for our published release bundles (CycloneDX format) and GPG-signed release artifacts.
  * For air-gapped installs we provide a signed bundle and a checksum manifest. Customer may independently verify signatures.

I'll attach the Appendix A PDF with the SBOM summary and a short checklist for signature verification.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Principal Product Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: RFI_Starlab_Appendix_A.pdf (SBOM + attestation checklist)

Tina — operator access and runbook summary below, attached is operator_runbook_draft.docx. Quick points: 

- Access model:
  * No persistent inbound SSH from the internet. Operator access is provided from a customer-controlled bastion/jump host. For airgapped installs operators work from an on-prem console inside the isolated network.
  * Temporary access: for vendor-assisted upgrades, we use ephemeral certificates (certs expire after configured TTL) and require MFA + one-time access tokens. All vendor sessions are recorded and logged to customer telemetry.

- On-call and maintenance windows:
  * Standard maintenance cadence: quarterly patch windows for noncritical updates, emergency patch workflows documented for CVEs rated critical.
  * We include a 30/60/90-day upgrade plan for the first three months post-install to allow staged validation.

- Training: we offer a 2-day on-site operator workshop for airgapped installs (ops runbook walkthrough + failover drills) or remote instructor-led sessions for VPC installs.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Manager, Field Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachments: operator_runbook_draft.docx

Summary:
- Network: Customer-controlled egress by default; we provide a minimal allow-list if you choose to enable telemetry. Air-gapped installs supported via signed bundles and removable media.
- Keys: Customer-managed KMS recommended; HSM options available under an MSP arrangement. Keys for runtime encryption are rotated locally and never exfiltrated.
- Operator access: Bastion-based, ephemeral certs for vendor-assisted sessions, full session recording.
- Supply chain: SBOMs in CycloneDX, signed artifacts and checksum manifests for air-gapped distribution.
- Training & ops: 2-day on-site workshop available; standard quarterly maintenance cadence with documented emergency patch playbook.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm if you want a fully air-gapped installation or a customer-managed egress VPC install so we can tailor the SOW.
2) If possible, schedule a 45-minute clarifying call next week — we are available Tue/Wed 5/19-5/20 09:00-12:00 PT.
3) Once you confirm the installation mode we will produce a short SOW addendum and an operator-training estimate.

Thanks for the quick turnaround window — we look forward to the call.
